question: What is the normal resting heart rate range for a healthy adult?
explanation: A resting heart rate between 60 and 100 beats per minute is standard for normal adult physiological function. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which part of the heart acts as the natural pacemaker?
explanation: You've got this! The sinoatrial (SA) node is the heart's natural pacemaker because it fires off the electrical signals that start every heartbeat. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which cranial nerve helps slow down the heart rate?
explanation: Great try! The vagus nerve is the main highway for the parasympathetic system to tell the heart to slow down and relax. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h2)

question: How does the sympathetic nervous system ("fight or flight") affect the heart?

options.A: It stops pacemaker activity until rest resumes
options.B: It slows down electrical conduction through the atria
options.C: It increases heart rate and enhances contractility
options.D: It decreases heart rate and lowers blood pressure

explanation: Think about how your heart races when you're scared or excited! The sympathetic system pumps out adrenaline to make the heart beat faster and stronger. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h2)

question: What heart rate means an adult has tachycardia (a fast heart rate)?
explanation: Remember, anything over 100 beats per minute at rest is called tachycardia. You'll hear this term a lot in the ward! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why might a fit athlete have a resting heart rate of 50 beats per minute and still be totally healthy?

options.A: Their heart pumps a larger stroke volume with each beat
options.B: Their body tissues require less oxygen than a normal person
options.C: Their sinoatrial node fires at a slower fixed rate
options.D: Their parasympathetic tone is permanently blocked by exercise

explanation: An athlete's heart is strong! It pumps out so much blood with every single beat that it doesn't need to beat as often to keep the body happy. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h3)

question: Where is the best spot on the chest to listen to the apical pulse?

options.A: Second intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.B: Third intercostal space at the right midclavicular line
options.C: Fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line
options.D: Fourth intercostal space at the left sternal border

explanation: Picture placing your stethoscope just below the left nipple area—that's roughly the 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line where the heart apex beats loudest! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h4)

question: When should you listen to the apical pulse for a full minute instead of just checking the wrist?

options.A: When checking circulation after a cast is applied
options.B: When the patient is sleeping quietly in bed
options.C: When the patient has a known irregular rhythm
options.D: When measuring routine vital signs in a healthy adult

explanation: If a patient's heartbeat is skipping or irregular, a quick wrist pulse can miss beats. Listening right at the chest for a full minute gives you the true picture. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h4)

question: Which of these common body changes will naturally make the heart beat faster?
explanation: Fever makes your body's engine run faster! For every degree your temperature goes up, your heart rate naturally climbs too. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which of the following does NOT cause a fast heart rate (tachycardia)?
explanation: Remember, the vagus nerve is your body's brake pedal. Stimulating it slows the heart down rather than speeding it up! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h5)

question: A patient's heart rate is 120 beats per minute, and they feel dizzy and short of breath. What is the nurse's best first step?

options.A: Apply warm blankets to the lower extremities
options.B: Administer a sleeping pill to calm the patient down
options.C: Document the finding as normal baseline variation
options.D: Assess blood pressure and check for signs of poor perfusion

explanation: Safety first! When a fast heart rate starts causing dizziness, we need to check right away if their blood pressure and circulation are holding up. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which emergency drug is commonly given to treat a dangerously slow heart rate?
explanation: Atropine is the go-to emergency drug for symptomatic bradycardia. It blocks the vagus nerve to quickly speed the heart back up. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h6)
